sourcedFrom: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page (2019 — revision "015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019" on the back page)
cleanIntro:
The LWRCI SMG-45 is a .45 ACP pistol-caliber carbine with AR-style lower controls but no AR inside: it runs on a delayed-blowback / short-recoil system in which a yoke links the breech block to the barrel for the first part of the recoil stroke, and it feeds from HK-UMP magazines.

The one thing an AR owner must unlearn is the takedown: the SMG does not hinge open. Both takedown pins come all the way out and the lower pulls straight away from the upper; the stock assembly then slides off the back and the whole recoil assembly slides out the rear. LWRCI's routine maintenance follows every firing session; its detailed maintenance — the recoil assembly and breech block apart — comes every 1,000 rounds or weekly in the field.

steps.title: Muzzle safe — magazine out
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction and keep it there. Press the magazine release lever away from the trigger guard and pull the magazine out of the well.
steps.prose: With a magazine still seated, working the charging handle only chambers the next round.
steps.quote: While pointing the muzzle in a safe direction, remove the magazine (if present) by depressing the magazine release and pulling the magazine out.
steps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing Your Weapon, printed p.12

steps.title: Hold the bolt catch down
steps.action: Press and hold the bottom half of either bolt catch lever. The controls are ambidextrous, so either side works.
steps.prose: Holding the lower half of the catch is what traps the breech block to the rear when you draw it back.
steps.quote: Press and hold the bottom half of either bolt catch lever.
steps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing Your Weapon, printed p.12

steps.title: Charging handle all the way back
steps.action: With the other hand, grasp the charging handle, press its latch and pull the handle and breech block firmly all the way to the rear. Any chambered round ejects; the breech block is trapped by the bolt catch.
steps.prose: Short of the full stroke the bolt catch has nothing to hold, and the breech block runs home again.
steps.quote: grasp the charging handle, depress the latch(es) and firmly pull the charging handle and breech block all the way to the rear.
steps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing Your Weapon, printed p.12

steps.title: Let go of the charging handle
steps.action: Release the charging handle. The breech block stays locked to the rear on the bolt catch.
steps.prose: The handle is non-reciprocating, so it does not ride with the breech block.
steps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing Your Weapon, printed p.13

steps.title: LOOK into the chamber
steps.action: Roll the carbine counter-clockwise until you can see the bolt and chamber through the ejection port. See an empty chamber and a bolt locked to the rear. In poor light, check by feel.
steps.prose: No case flying out is not proof of an empty chamber — the look is the check.
steps.caution: Do not depend on the fact that no casing was ejected on clearing.
steps.quote: Visually check to make sure that the chamber is clear and that the bolt is locked to the rear.
steps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing Your Weapon, printed p.13

steps.title: Clear it again before anything comes apart
steps.action: Repeat the clearing check more than once before the charging handle or any pin moves.
steps.prose: LWRCI opens its field strip with this step because disassembly and cleaning are where negligent discharges happen.
steps.quote: Clear the firearm several times. Most negligent discharges occur during disassembly and cleaning operations.
steps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.20

steps.title: Charging handle: hold it at 90 degrees and compress
steps.action: With the breech block home and the gun still assembled, grasp the folded-out charging handle and push it in against its spring while holding it at its 90-degree angle — it compresses about half an inch. Do not rotate it.
steps.prose: LWRCI says the motion is not obvious the first time and becomes simple with practice; the fully assembled gun is the easiest place to do it.
steps.quote: Grasp the charging handle and compress the spring while maintaining the 90 degree angle.
steps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.20

steps.title: Charging handle straight out the side
steps.action: Holding the handle compressed, pull it straight out of the side of the upper receiver. No twist at any point.
steps.prose: Twisting is what binds it; straight out is the whole technique.
steps.quote: When the handle is compressed, pull it directly out of the side of the upper receiver. Do not twist or rotate the charging handle during removal.
steps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.21

steps.title: Both takedown pins out to their stops
steps.action: From the left side, press in the front and the rear takedown pins. From the right side, pull each one until it stops. A tight pin is normal from the factory — a punch and hammer can knock it through.
steps.prose: Both pins come out. The SMG does not hinge on the front pin the way an AR does.
steps.caution: THE LWRCI SMG DOES NOT PIVOT OPEN LIKE AN AR-STYLE FIREARM. ATTEMPTING TO PIVOT THE FIREARM AROUND THE FRONT TAKEDOWN PIN CAN RESULT IN DAMAGE TO THE UPPER OR LOWER.
steps.quote: From the left-hand side, press in the front and rear takedown pins. From the right-hand side, pull the pins until they stop, indicating that they are fully extended.
steps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.21

steps.title: Lower straight off — no pivot
steps.action: Pull the lower receiver straight away from the upper.
steps.prose: Levering it open around the front pin is the one move that damages this gun on the bench.
steps.quote: Pull the lower straight away from the upper to remove it.
steps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.21

steps.title: Stock assembly off the back
steps.action: With the lower off, slide the stock assembly free of the rear of the upper.
steps.prose: The lower and the stock are now field stripped; the recoil assembly is still in the upper.
steps.quote: slide the stock assembly free of the upper
steps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.21

steps.title: Yoke down to unlocked
steps.action: If the breech block will not drop free, pull the locking yoke toward the bottom of the upper. Rocking the barrel back and forth usually lets it drop.
steps.prose: While the yoke is up, the breech block is still linked to the barrel and will not come out.
steps.quote: The locking yoke inside the upper receiver must be in its unlocked position for the barrel and breech block to be separated.
steps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.22

steps.title: Recoil assembly out the rear
steps.action: Slide the whole recoiling assembly — breech block, action spring and guide rod — out of the rear of the upper receiver.
steps.prose: Keep it in one piece for now; it comes apart in Deep Clean.
steps.quote: Once the charging handle is removed and the locking yoke is in the unlocked position, the entire recoiling assembly will slide freely out of the rear of the upper receiver, completing the field strip.
steps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.22

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: upper receiver with barrel, recoil assembly, charging handle, lower receiver and stock assembly. DEEP CLEAN carries LWRCI's detailed disassembly — the recoil assembly apart and the firing pin out of the breech block.
steps.prose: LWRCI's own limit: nothing beyond its field strip and detailed disassembly outside the factory or a gunsmith's shop.
steps.quote: Please note that rifles should not be broken down beyond the field strip unless in a controlled environment, such as the factory or in a gunsmith’s shop.
steps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.20

deepSteps.title: Bumper off the guide rod
deepSteps.action: Compress the action spring away from the rubber bumper at the end of the guide rod. With the tension off, slide the guide rod down the channel in the bumper to free the bumper.
deepSteps.prose: Keep the spring compressed in your hand until the bumper is clear.
deepSteps.quote: Compress the action spring away from the rubber bumper. Once spring tension has been relieved, slide the guide rod down in the channel on the bumper to release the bumper from the guide rod.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.22

deepSteps.title: Ease the spring off — breech block off the rod
deepSteps.action: Let the compressed action spring out slowly. The spring and the breech block slide off the guide rod.
deepSteps.prose: A spring let go all at once launches itself across the room.
deepSteps.quote: Carefully release the compressed action spring. The spring and breech block will slide off of the guide rod.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.22

deepSteps.title: Extension off the breech block
deepSteps.action: Separate the breech block from its extension by pushing on the top surface of the extension near the locking lugs.
deepSteps.prose: It slides; it does not need prying.
deepSteps.quote: The breech block and extension are separated by pushing on the top surface of the extension near the locking lugs.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.22

deepSteps.title: Firing pin a quarter-turn
deepSteps.action: Twist the back end of the firing pin 90 degrees, either direction. A front sight adjustment tool fits the grooves on the pin if fingers will not turn it.
deepSteps.prose: The quarter-turn unlocks the pin from behind the firing pin block.
deepSteps.quote: To remove the firing pin and firing pin block, twist the back end of the firing pin 90 degrees in either direction.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.23

deepSteps.title: Firing pin, block and springs out
deepSteps.action: Draw the firing pin and its spring out of the back of the breech block. With the pin out, the firing pin block and its spring come free too.
deepSteps.prose: Two springs, two parts — keep each spring with its own part.
deepSteps.quote: The firing pin and spring can now move backwards out of the breech block (5.3.H). Once the firing pin is removed, the firing pin block and spring will come free of the breech block as well.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.23

deepSteps.title: Barrel stays in — LWRCI's stopping point
deepSteps.action: Stop here. The barrel stays in the upper for cleaning.
deepSteps.prose: LWRCI's book does carry barrel removal, but only for extreme fouling: the barrel's position is set at the factory by a dog-point set screw, and re-setting that screw with threadlocker is critical to how the gun runs.
deepSteps.quote: The barrel assembly should be removed only to address extreme fouling, not for routine maintenance.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI SMG Pistol Caliber Carbine — Operator's Manual — 015-0023 Revision A 06.23.2019 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.23

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Solvent-soaked patch on a cleaning rod, pushed from the chamber end to the muzzle; let the barrel sit for several minutes.
Bore brush on the rod: punch the bore several times to break the build-up free.
Dry patches through the bore until they come out clean.
Check that the barrel reciprocates freely in the upper.

cleaning.name: BREECH BLOCK AND RECOIL ASSEMBLY
tasks: Wipe the outside of the recoil assembly with a cloth slightly dampened with solvent.
Scrub the bolt face with a nylon brush dipped in solvent.
Deep clean: scrub the recoil assembly with a nylon brush and solvent; carbon-cutting solvent for hard carbon.
Moderate coat of lube on the breech block, especially the surfaces that face down, and along the whole outside of the spring guide tube.
A few drops on the rear of the firing pin and inside the firing pin block, worked in by moving the pin and block.
Do not lubricate the bolt face.
Do not use water-based lubricants such as WD-40 — LWRCI says the water content can aid corrosion.

cleaning.name: UPPER RECEIVER
tasks: Wipe the inside of the upper receiver with a solvent-damp cloth.
Deep clean: scrub the inside of the upper with a nylon brush and solvent, then wipe it dry.
Coat of lube inside the upper, especially the horizontal surfaces the breech block runs on, such as the top of the ejector housing.

cleaning.name: CHARGING HANDLE AND PINS
tasks: Wipe the charging handle and coat its outside with lube.

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Check each magazine is clean and not dented or cracked, the feed lips are not bent, and the follower moves freely and returns under its own spring.
Do not oil or lubricate magazines or ammunition.

reassembly: Deep clean only: firing pin block spring into its seat, firing pin block over it; firing pin spring over the firing pin and the pin in through the block into the breech block; push the pin in and turn it 90 degrees to lock it behind the block.

Deep clean only: breech block extension slid back up onto the breech block; breech block onto the spring guide tube; action spring onto the guide tube and into the breech block, held compressed; bumper back on with its slot over the flats at the end of the tube, then let the spring seat into it.

Recoil assembly into the rear of the upper and forward until the breech block is in battery. If it will not go, the firing pin is mis-clocked — twist it slightly until its notches line up and the block slides in.
Stock assembly slid back into place behind the upper; the bumper may need a slight push to let it seat.
⛔ Do not pivot the lower on the front pin — line it up straight and push both takedown pins back in; a non-marring brass or nylon hammer may be needed for snug pins.
Charging handle pushed back in from either side.
Run the function check before loading.
fncheck: Clear the carbine first. Seat an empty magazine and tug it to be sure the catch holds it. Pull the charging handle back: the breech block must lock to the rear on the empty magazine and the handle must not come forward on its own — return it home. Drop the magazine; the breech block stays back. Press the large upper paddle of either bolt release: the breech block slams forward into battery (never onto a chamber flag). On SAFE, pull the trigger — the hammer must not fall. On SEMI, pull it — the hammer drops with a loud click. Charge it again holding the trigger down, then release the trigger slowly: you should hear the disconnector click and the hammer must stay cocked. Then clear the carbine again.
